candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 24:15-19. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. Mt 2:2.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On Balaam's fourth oracle — 'I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel' (Num 24:17) — Ephrem reads the doubled-image (Star + Sceptre) as the canonical Old-Testament prophecy of the Messiah's advent: the Star is the sign that appears to the Gentile Magi (Mt 2:2 — 'we have seen his star in the east'), the Sceptre is the Davidic kingship received by the Son of David. The Gentile diviner Balaam prophesies through gritted teeth the salvation of the world. Tewahedo nativity-iconography cites Num 24:17 as the canonical Old-Testament doubled-anchor of the Star-of-Bethlehem and the Davidic-Solomonic Sceptre — both inherited by the Tewahedo Solomonic dynasty's self-understanding.

On Balaam's fourth oracle — 'I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel' (Num 24:17) — Ephrem reads the doubled-image (Star + Sceptre) as the canonical Old-Testament prophecy of the Messiah's advent: the Star is the sign that appears to the Gentile Magi (Mt 2:2 — 'we have seen his star in the east'), the Sceptre is the Davidic kingship received by the Son of David. The Gentile diviner Balaam prophesies through gritted teeth the salvation of the world. Tewahedo nativity-iconography cites Num 24:17 as the canonical Old-Testament doubled-anchor of the Star-of-Bethlehem and the Davidic-Solomonic Sceptre — both inherited by the Tewahedo Solomonic dynasty's self-understanding.
